source_decompilation: read-only Ghidra decompilation of the pinned library at each record's address; temporary analysis output is not required to reproduce this inventory
scope: 22 active standard-NetFn override records plus 2 Group Extension override records; table terminators excluded
record_format: 16-byte records: command at +0, minimum privilege at +1, handler pointer at +4, request length or 0xff at +8, mask 0xaaaa at +10, interface selector 0 at +12
activation_note: Normal-LUN records are present in Fujitsu's OEM handler map, but individual LAN reachability is not established by this static inventory. LUN-3 storage records have a static LUN-3 dispatch map; a prior valid LAN LUN-3 request returned completion 0xc0, so remote execution is unproven.

records.request_length: 0 exact (handler)
records.response: 16 bytes including CC on success
records.deviation: Returns Fujitsu-populated device ID and product fields.

records.request_length: 0 exact (handler)
records.response: 17 bytes including CC plus 16-byte GUID on success
records.deviation: Selects and may byte-swap a configured Fujitsu GUID; mutex-protected cache.

records.request_length: variable table; handler reads user selector byte0 and calls strlen(request+1) without validating request length or a NUL terminator
records.response: one-byte CC 00 when Fujitsu configuration write succeeds; standard SetUserName response only when that write fails
records.deviation: Fujitsu writes config at index (request[0]&0x3f)-1 using strlen-derived username length; a successful write returns before standard SetUserName validation. User selector low six bits 0 underflows the computed index. The unbounded strlen can read past malformed request data.
records.side_effect: user identity mutation; malformed-input out-of-bounds read candidate and standard-validation bypass on successful config write
records.activation: normal OEM map; static; Admin table privilege still applies
records.certainty: handler decompiled at 0x00028c90; backend index handling and exploitability unproven

records.request_length: exactly 3 or 11 bytes (handler); byte0 low nibble selects LAN channel, byte1 high two bits select operation 0/1/2 and bits4-5 must be zero
records.response: operation 1 returns [00,current_alert_status]; operations 0/2 return one-byte CC; C7 other lengths, CC invalid channel/operation bits, D3 unmapped LAN interface, 81 alert already pending, CE async post failure
records.deviation: Operation 1 reads per-interface alert status; operation 2 clears that status to zero (does not accept a replacement value); operation 0 sets status FF, builds alert from request or destination type, posts asynchronously, and restores status 01 if posting fails.
records.side_effect: operation 0 may send network alert; operation 2 clears alert-status byte
records.activation: normal OEM map; static; CC 00 on posted alert does not prove delivery
records.certainty: handler decompiled at 0x00036bec; downstream network delivery unproven

records.request_length: variable table; handler ignores request
records.response: 6 bytes including CC, count unit 05 and count LE32
records.deviation: Reads Fujitsu battery-backed POH register and scales it.

records.request_length: 1 exact (table): action
records.response: CC only
records.deviation: Standard actions 00-05 plus Fujitsu 0d forced-off override and 0e pulse power button; queues actuation asynchronously.
records.certainty: handler decompiled; physical actuation not implied by CC 00

records.request_length: variable table; standard Set System Boot Options format
records.response: standard handler response or CC 82 for selected parameters and platform state
records.deviation: Serializes boot-option setting with mutex; parameter 04 can signal semaphore; parameters 03/05 can be blocked by platform state.

records.request_length: variable table; at least group byte; dc branch requires 2 including group
records.response: dc: standard DCMI capabilities; 52: CC, group byte, 1, 32-byte fingerprint on success
records.deviation: Group dc delegates to standard DCMI Get Capabilities. Fujitsu group 52 ('R') selector 01 returns a certificate fingerprint only for Admin and channel 0f; other group IDs return CC c1.
records.certainty: handler decompiled; 52 branch not live tested

records.request_length: variable table; at least group byte; dc branch requires 4 including group; 52 leaf requires at least 2 bytes [52,selector]
records.response: dc: 19 bytes including CC per existing analysis; 52: 2 bytes [cc,52] on short/channel/config error, otherwise always 34 bytes [cc,52,32 body bytes]. Username/password body is copied only after both createNewUser and follow-up config write succeed; failure can still return 34 bytes with body not filled, and config-write failure may retain CC 00 after deleting the user.
records.deviation: Group dc delegates to standard DCMI Get Power Reading. Fujitsu group 52 enters Redfish host-interface bootstrap for any second byte, not only a5. A non-a5 selector first clears the bootstrap config flag, then still attempts user creation. Admin context and channel 0f are required; never probe as a read.
records.side_effect: dc is read; 52 creates a privileged user, may clear bootstrap flag, and can return credentials
records.activation: normal group-extension OEM map; 52 branch static only, LAN channel rejected by leaf
records.certainty: GroupExtension02@0x0003db3c and GroupRedfishCmd02@0x0003dd40 decompiled; 52 branch not live tested

branches.request: [52,selector] length>=2; a5 preserves bootstrap flag, any other selector clears it before user creation
branches.safety: HIGH: creates/deletes user, changes bootstrap flag, may return credentials; static only
